title: Cocos AI attested TLS can retain trust after workload state changes
summary: A peer continues to trust a long-lived TLS connection after an attacker changes the attested workload code, memory-backed state or configuration. Attestation at connection establishment does not establish freshness for the connection lifetime.

severity.rationale: An attacker must already be able to modify attested workload state after the connection is established. This local-access prerequisite and specialized attestation configuration warrant a 30-day response.

affected.note: The advisory lists versions through 0.8.2 inclusive.

exposure: Applications relying on Cocos AI intra-handshake attested TLS for ongoing workload trust are exposed when an attacker can modify the attester state without closing the connection. Long-lived connections increase the stale-evidence window.

params.instructions: Check the resolved github.com/ultravioletrs/cocos module and attested TLS usage. The advisory lists versions through 0.8.2 as affected and 0.9.0 as patched; verify any intervening version with the vendor.

remediation.action: Update Cocos and maintain evidence freshness
remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.9.0 or later, the listed patched version. The advisory proposes periodic or operator-defined post-handshake re-attestation as a workaround.
remediation.risk: Medium. Upgrading and introducing re-attestation can change connection behavior and require integration validation.

verification: Confirm the resolved Cocos module is at least 0.9.0 and the attestation configuration meets the application's evidence-freshness requirements.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from the directly inspected reviewed advisory for independent review.
